sources: DEMO-0001 - Demo Assy, Valve Manifold, Type A, Rev A (demo document)
DEMO-0002 - Demo Assy, Valve Manifold, Type B, Rev A (demo document)
notes: ALL CONTENT IN THIS FILE IS FICTIONAL. The product, the part list, the operation sequence, the checks and the storage locations are invented for this interface prototype. Nothing here describes any real product, process, document, employer or workplace.

Steps follow DEMO-0001 (Type A) numbering. Type B is identical except: step 18 uses flow plate DM-1011-B, step 22 uses adapter block DM-1013-B, step 26 uses cover DM-1021-B, and step 27 places the finished manifold on the outfeed cart instead of fastening it to the demo bracket.

Torque values are deliberately written as 'the value on the station card' rather than numbers. This is a demo of an interface, not a work instruction, and no real torque figure appears anywhere in this project.
photoFilename paths point to files in the part-photos/ folder. The folder ships empty; the app shows a 'Photo pending' placeholder until a photo is added.

parts.name: Manifold Body, Lower
parts.whatItIs: Cast aluminium lower half of the demo manifold. Carries the inlet and outlet ports and mates to the upper body across the interface gasket.

parts.name: Manifold Body, Upper
parts.whatItIs: Cast aluminium upper half. Holds the cartridge bores and the relief spring pocket.

parts.name: O-Ring, Port, Small
parts.whatItIs: Small nitrile o-ring used on the two signal ports.

parts.name: O-Ring, Port, Large
parts.whatItIs: Large nitrile o-ring used on the inlet and outlet ports.

parts.name: Backup Ring, PTFE
parts.whatItIs: Thin PTFE ring that sits behind each large o-ring so it cannot extrude under test pressure.

parts.name: Retainer Clip
parts.whatItIs: Spring steel clip that locks a cartridge valve into its bore.

parts.name: Screw, Socket Head, Short
parts.whatItIs: Short socket head screw used on the retainer clips and the serial tag plate.

parts.name: Gasket, Interface
parts.whatItIs: Die-cut gasket between the upper and lower manifold bodies.

parts.name: Cartridge Valve, Inlet
parts.whatItIs: Screw-in cartridge that meters flow into the manifold. Identified by the single groove on its hex.

parts.name: Cartridge Valve, Outlet
parts.whatItIs: Screw-in cartridge on the return side. Identified by two grooves on its hex.

parts.name: Flow Plate
parts.whatItIs: Plate that sets which internal passage is open. Type A and Type B builds use different plates.

parts.name: Stud, Port Adapter
parts.whatItIs: Threaded stud that joins the port adapter block to the lower body.

parts.name: Port Adapter Block
parts.whatItIs: Block that converts the manifold ports to the demo test fittings. Type A and Type B use different blocks.

parts.name: Washer, Fiber
parts.whatItIs: Fiber sealing washer under the adapter stud.

parts.name: Tag Plate, Serial
parts.whatItIs: Blank metal tag the assembler marks and fits to the finished manifold.

parts.name: Screw, Flat Head Socket
parts.whatItIs: Flat head screw used on the flow plate.

parts.name: Shim, Adapter
parts.whatItIs: Thin shim that sets the adapter block standoff.

parts.name: Bushing, Guide
parts.whatItIs: Pressed bushing that guides the relief spring stack.

parts.name: Spring, Relief
parts.whatItIs: Coil spring for the demo relief circuit.

parts.name: Screw, Button Head Socket
parts.whatItIs: Button head screw used on the manifold cover.

parts.name: Cover, Manifold
parts.whatItIs: Snap-on cover over the cartridge bores. Type A and Type B use different covers.

parts.name: Screw, Mount
parts.whatItIs: Screw that fastens the finished manifold to the demo bracket.

assemblySteps.instruction: Draw (1) DM-1001 lower body and (1) DM-1002 upper body from the demo shelf and set both on the prep mat with the port faces up.
Inspect both castings for burrs around every port opening. Any burr you can catch a fingernail on gets knocked down with the deburr tool before the parts go any further.
Wash both bodies in the parts washer basket, then blow the passages dry with the air gun. Safety glasses are required whenever the air gun is in use.
Set the two clean bodies on the build fixture. The lower body goes in the front pocket, the upper body in the rear pocket.
Grease and fit (2) DM-1003 small o-rings into the two signal ports on the lower body. Rings must sit flat in the groove with no twist.
Fit (1) DM-1005 PTFE backup ring into each of the two large port grooves, flat side toward the port opening.
Grease and fit (2) DM-1004 large o-rings on top of the backup rings. Seat each ring fully with the plastic pick, never with a metal tool.
Seal check: run a fingertip around all four ring grooves. Every ring should be below the face of the casting. A ring standing proud means it is twisted; pull it and refit.
Press (2) DM-1018 guide bushings into the spring pockets of the upper body. Keep the guard down on the press and use both activation buttons.
Check with the depth gauge that each bushing is flush to just below the pocket face. If a bushing stands proud, press it again rather than tapping it.
Drop (2) DM-1019 relief springs into the bushings. Springs must drop freely under their own weight; a spring that hangs up means a bushing is cocked.
Fit (1) DM-1008 interface gasket over the locating pins on the lower body. The wide tab faces the front of the fixture.
Hand-start (1) DM-1009 inlet cartridge into the inlet bore. The inlet cartridge is the one with a single groove on the hex. Never start a cartridge with a driver.
Torque the inlet cartridge to the value on the station card, then fit (1) DM-1006 retainer clip and secure it with (1) DM-1007 short screw.
Hand-start (1) DM-1010 outlet cartridge into the outlet bore. This one carries two grooves on the hex. Torque it to the value on the station card.
Fit the second DM-1006 retainer clip over the outlet cartridge and secure it with a DM-1007 short screw.
Cartridge check: both hex grooves must face the front of the fixture when the cartridges are fully seated. If a groove points anywhere else, back the cartridge out and reseat it.
Fit (1) DM-1011 flow plate across the two cartridge bores. Type A builds take DM-1011; Type B builds take DM-1011-B, which carries an extra slot on the right edge.
Secure the flow plate with (2) DM-1016 flat head screws torqued to the value on the station card.
Fit (1) DM-1017 adapter shim onto the lower body boss. One shim per build unless the traveller calls for two.
Add thread locker to (1) DM-1012 adapter stud, fit (1) DM-1014 fiber washer, and hand-start the stud into the boss.
Set (1) DM-1013 port adapter block over the stud and torque the stud to the value on the station card. Type A builds take DM-1013; Type B builds take DM-1013-B, which has the offset fitting.
Lower the upper body onto the lower body and close the fixture clamp. The two bodies should meet with no visible gap at the gasket line.
Move the assembly to the test bench and connect the demo test fittings. Bring the bench to test pressure and hold for the dwell time shown on the bench display.

Leak check: watch all four port faces and the gasket line for the full dwell. Any bubble at any location fails the unit. Failed units go on the red rework shelf with a fault tag, not back into the build queue.

Function check: cycle the bench lever three times. The relief should open and reseat on every cycle, and the lever should return on its own. Then fit (1) DM-1021 cover (DM-1021-B on Type B builds) and secure it with (2) DM-1020 button head screws.

Mark your initials and the build date on (1) DM-1015 serial tag plate, fit it with (1) DM-1007 short screw, then: Type A builds fasten the manifold to the demo bracket with (2) DM-1022 mount screws torqued to the value on the station card. Type B builds place the finished manifold on the outfeed cart.
